text: This is the sixth Environmental, Social and Governance ('ESG') Report of the Group, covering its management approach and performance on environmental and social aspects. This report is published in both Chinese and English. In case of any discrepancy between the two versions, the English version shall prevail. For governance section, please refer to the Corporate Governance Report on Pages 64 to 89 of the Annual Report.

This report is prepared in compliance with Environmental, Social and Governance Reporting Guide set out in Appendix 27 to the Rules Governing the Listing of Securities on the Stock Exchange (the 'Listing Rules'). We have followed the reporting principles of Materiality, Quantitative, Balance and Consistency in preparing this report.
Materiality:
Sustainability issues material to the Company are identified after stakeholder engagement every year.
Quantitative:
Data are presented in a manner conducive to year-on-year comparison in order to provide clarity about progress in addressing sustainability issues.
Balance:
The Company strives to report its positive as well as negative impacts along with steps it is taking to improve its ESG performance.
Consistency:
Consistency of data, including comparability with data for previous periods, is maintained to facilitate meaningful comparison over time.

The boundary of this report follows that of the annual report, which covers the Group's operations comprising air freight and ocean freight services in Hong Kong and Shanghai for the financial year from 1 January 2021 to 31 December 2021.

YTO Express (International) Holdings Limited ('YTO Express' or the 'Company', together with its subsidiaries, the 'Group'), formerly known as On Time Logistics Holdings Limited, is an international logistics operator established in 2013, headquartered in Hong Kong. On Time Group, a subsidiary of YTO Express, was founded in 1995. As a leading international logistic services provider, the Group's core business has been focusing on air and ocean freight forwarding and international express and parcel services, followed by its ancillary and contract logistics services as well as other businesses.

The air freight forwarding business continues to be the largest business of the Group. This involves arranging shipments by air according to booking instructions of customers, obtaining cargo space from airlines, preparing the relevant documentation, cargo handling, customs clearance at destination and delivery to the designated recipient. In this segment, we are well-recognised and regularly receive accolades from international organisations and major airlines. The Group will continue to deliver more targeted and high-quality international logistic services to customers.

The outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic has resulted in a significant acceleration in the growth of e-commerce and digital payments across the globe. The Group continues to seize opportunities in this fast-growing market to expand its business in international express and parcel services.

Considering our vision is to become a leading integrated logistic services provider, we intend to continuously enhance and refine our business strategies to expand our market share, striving to meet the needs of our customers and deal with new challenges under shifting market trends.

The Group understands the importance of aligning its business strategy with environmental and social concerns. We gradually embed sustainability factors into decision making, ensuring we could mitigate our environmental impacts while growing our business.

Management of risks and opportunities associated with sustainability has become board level matter and therefore we have set up an ESG Committee comprising of senior management to formulate ESG-related strategies, policies and targets. Our Environmental and Social Responsibility Policy delegates ESG related responsibilities and specifies objectives to all parties associated with the Group including its subsidiaries, associated companies and affiliates.

The ESG Committee regularly reports progress and performance in ESG matters to the Board of Directors while the Board oversees ESG risks and opportunities. Looking ahead, the Group might broaden the composition of the existing committee to enhance its ESG management.

Effective management of environmental, social and ethical risks the freight forwarding business faces is a prime concern of the Group and to address this issue, we use internal controls and risk management systems. The Board of Directors is responsible for identifying ESG risks including climate-related risks, whereas the management is responsible for evaluating the effectiveness of the internal control and risk management system and reports to the Board and the Audit Committee on a yearly basis. The Group incorporates material ESG topics in its management system to ensure effective risk management.

The Company's Board of Directors confirms that it has reviewed and approved the report. To the best of its knowledge, this report fairly addresses the identified material issues and presents the ESG management approach and performance of the Company.

The Group recognises the importance to communicate with all stakeholders including employees, suppliers, agents, partners, customers, shareholders, investors, government and non-governmental organisations. The Environmental and Social Responsibility Policy clearly stipulates the Group's responsibility for stakeholder communication:

1. Identify and engage stakeholders
2. Make due provision for interests and needs of all stakeholders
3. Communicate the Group's commitments and performance relating to sustainability responsibility
4. Ensure the Group's activities respect, promote and advance the identified principles for consumer rights and obligations
5. Be responsible for impacts associated with the Group's distribution of goods and services
6. Bear the responsibility for the Group's actions and omissions to its stakeholders
7. Respond to legitimate stakeholder claims
8. Be transparent about the actions and communicate progress made with regard to social responsibility performance
9. Consistently disclose the material information fully and accurately in a timely and verifiable manner
On an on-going basis, the Group evaluates the effectiveness of the communication processes. We engage with both internal and external stakeholders through communication channels listed below.

A materiality assessment is carried out every alternate year to identify issues that are most material to the Group and its stakeholders. An independent consultancy firm is engaged for that. Following the HKEX ESG Reporting Guide and taking GRI Standards into account, we follow a four-step approach of identification, prioritisation, validation and review in materiality assessment.

A total of 26 potential topics were marked in the assessment covering environmental, social and operational aspects. A questionnaire was administered online to internal stakeholders to collect their opinions on these material topics. Based on opinions received, the 26 identified issues were prioritised into four levels. The most pertinent topics (Level I) of the Group included anti-corruption, precautionary measures of child/forced labour, operating compliance and protection of intellectual property rights. The final results were reviewed and validated by the management of the Group.

At YTO Express, we are devoted to mitigating the impacts of our business on the environment and assess our environmental performance regularly. The Group's environmental management system is certified under ISO 14001:2015 standard. Environmental protection measures and their respective outcomes are reviewed regularly. The Group strives to achieve air and GHG emissions reduction, minimise waste generation and conserve energy, water and materials consumption.

To ensure continuous improvement in our environmental performance, we have set targets for different aspects of environmental protection and monitor our performance against these targets regularly. These are as shown in the table below:

Aspect | Target
GHG emissions | Implement emissions reduction measures annually.
Energy efficiency | Prefer to acquire electric equipment with energy efficiency label.
Water use | Prefer to acquire water related equipment with Grade 1 efficiency label.
Waste | Increase the use of recycled paper.

We are dedicated to making informed decisions and initiatives on environmental and related issues and act in accordance with relevant laws and regulations. During the year, the Group was not aware of any non-compliance with laws and regulations 1 that have a significant impact on the Group relating to air and greenhouse gases emissions, discharges into water and land, and generation of hazardous and non-hazardous waste.

The Group believes climate change needs to be addressed by all. We leave no stone unturned to identify the risks climate change implies for our business and aim to develop strategies on an ongoing basis, while following what our peers are doing. A Climate Change Policy has been formulated, which lists actions required and taken for addressing climate change.

Disclosure |  Ensure collection of reliable data of its Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions and ensure right calculations and documentation;  Disclose its GHG emissions and emission reduction actions annually;  Disclose its climate-related risks and opportunities.
Assessment |  Assess climate-related risks and opportunities regularly;  Address climate-related risks as part of its risk management process by adoption of effective mitigation measures.
Implementation |  Adopt energy efficient practices in its operations;  Implement eco-friendly practices in its procurement process; and  Encourage its employees to follow low-carbon practices in its daily operations.

Resources consumed in our operations include electricity, petrol, diesel, paper and water. Our operations do not involve the use of any packaging materials.

During the year, the Group consumed a total of 543.7 MWh of energy, with an energy intensity of 0.14 MWh per square meter. Electricity consumption was 405.4 MWh, which accounts for 75% of total energy consumption, and is attributed to the use of equipment at the office.

Greenhouse gas ('GHG') emissions from our business operations include direct emissions from fuel consumption (Scope 1), indirect emissions from the use of electricity (Scope 2) and other indirect emissions from business travel by air, paper disposal at landfills, freshwater processing and sewage treatment (Scope 3). During the year, the Group's total GHG emissions were 301.1 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent (tCO 2 e), with an emission intensity of 0.08 tCO 2 e per square meter of floor area. The GHG emissions were mainly contributed by emissions from the use of electricity, which constituted around 62% of total GHG emissions.

The Group continues to take a range of emissions reduction measures to manage and minimise air and GHG emissions from its operations. These measures include reducing the frequency of business travel by using online communication channels, replacing low energy-efficiency equipment with higher efficiency ones and optimising operations flow in warehouses.

The Group continues to follow a green office policy and has taken a range of measures for conserving energy, water and paper consumed in its operations to ensure efficient management and use of resources. Moreover, we reduce the use of carbon dependent energy sources and other natural resources by deploying more energy-efficient processes and green technologies. Guidelines on energy, water and paper-saving are provided to all employees. Through encouragement and education, we strive to drive behavioural changes for conserving energy and natural resources within the workplace.

Energy Saving | ■ Switch off all idle electronic appliances, lighting and air-conditioning when not in use ■ Use ower-saving mode in electronic appliances where applicable
Paper Saving | ■ Adopt paperless communication during internal meetings ■ Encourage the use of recycled paper, and printing both sides of the paper ■ Adopt electronic communications with external parties
Water Saving | ■ Post labels with water saving tips at the office

The Group's air emissions are mainly attributed to petrol and diesel combustion by vehicles. During the year, the Group's operations emitted 0.2 kg of sulphur oxides (SO x ), 25.4 kg of nitrogen oxides (NO x ) and 1.6 kg of respirable suspended particles (RSP).

To better manage and reduce air emissions, the Group controls the use of vehicles by enumerating clear guidelines. They include switching off idling engines, conducting regular vehicle maintenance and encouraging employees to travel by public transport. To continuously reduce emissions, the effectiveness of reduction measures is regularly reviewed.

The Group's operations generate hazardous waste comprising toner cartridges and fluorescent lamps and nonhazardous waste such as domestic waste. During the year, the Group generated a total of 0.05 tonnes of hazardous waste and 23.7 tonnes of non-hazardous waste. The hazardous and non-hazardous waste intensity by floor area were 0.000012 tonnes per square meter and 0.006 tonnes per square meter respectively.

The Group is committed to educating and training its staff to handle waste sustainably. For instance, recycling bins are placed in the office to facilitate recycling. They should always try to recycle and reuse materials before disposal, to the extent possible. Hazardous waste is regularly collected by a licensed waste collector, while non-hazardous waste is sent to landfills.

The Group adheres to internationally recognised environmental principles and commitments and strives to assess and manage the environmental impacts of its operations effectively. Being an environmentally responsible logistics operator, the Group advocates the use of green technology and collaborates with partners to promote sustainable logistics.

As of the end of December 2021, the Group employed 273 full-time staff, of which 116 or 42% are based in Hong Kong and 157 or 58% are based in Shanghai. The proportion of male to female is 1.02. In terms of age profile, 54% of our employees are aged 30-40 while 20% are aged under 30. About 27% of employees are at managerial level and 73% are general employees.

During the year, the overall employee turnover rate and new hire rate were 26% and 40% respectively.

The Group has a Recruitment and Hiring Policy in place to guide recruitment procedures and to ensure consistency. The recruitment process is transparent and fair. We select candidates solely on the basis of qualifications, experience and personal abilities. There are clear conditions and restrictions when an employee's relatives apply for an opening and the concerned applicant has to disclose that. This helps avoid preferential selection.

We offer career development opportunities to our employees, including internal transfers to fill up vacant positions to the extent possible. We have also set up standard guidelines for the promotion process to ensure consistency and fairness of the fixed promotion cycle. Regular and systematic reviews and evaluations of employees' performance form the basis for changes in employees' remuneration, including basic salary and promotion. This also facilitates communication between employees and the management concerning job requirements and performance.

Decisions on employee dismissal and termination are regulated by our internal guidelines to assure fairness. The HR Department carries out interviews of employees who resign to comprehend the reasons for resignation and to collect feedback. Involuntary termination of employment occurs only in case of serious misconduct or violation of the Group's policy.

The Group understands that employees are important assets and its business development depends on their hard work. To attract and retain talent, we offer competitive remuneration and welfare packages that include annual leave, marriage leave, maternity leave and paternity leave. We provide overtime allowance, including monetary compensation or compensatory leave, standby allowance, and taxi allowance for employees who work extra hours. Medical insurance scheme is in place for employees to enjoy medical benefits. To promote employees to be vaccinated against covid-19, we provide employees with a day off on the day of vaccination.

An Outstanding Staff Award recognises and honours distinguished contributions made by employees every year. Winners are chosen on the basis of performance, particularly if they are promoting a positive culture within the Group and have demonstrated the ability to discharge their duties in an exemplary manner. In order to appreciate dedicated employees, we have set up a share award scheme that allows employees to purchase the Group's shares at a price lower than the market price.

On March 8th, our female employees were recognized for their contributions to the company's everyday operations, and they were gifted beautiful roses, special presents and participated in special activities to celebrate International Women's Day.

The Group strives to create an equal and inclusive working environment free of discrimination or harassment. We have zero tolerance for any form of discrimination on the grounds of age, gender, race or religion. We also prohibit all unfair and discriminating employment practices. In order to maintain a diversified workplace, a Board Diversity Policy is in place to assess the Board composition under diversified perspectives including gender, age, cultural and educational background and professional experience. As an equal opportunity employer, we continue to provide equal opportunity in all aspects to all employees and ensure that labour practices followed are fair and ethical, and respect the fundamental human rights of all employees.

There are defined standard procedures for decisions on employment related activities, including various aspects such as salary, compensation and dismissal, recruitment, promotion and benefits, working hours and rest periods.

The Group was not aware of any non-compliance with relevant laws and regulations 2 that have a significant impact on the Group relating to compensation and dismissal, recruitment and promotion, working hours, rest periods, equal opportunity, diversity, anti-discrimination, and other benefits and welfare during the reporting period.

The Group ensures adherence to labour standards and prohibits all forms of unethical practices, which also applies to its suppliers and subcontractors. We take rigorous measures to prohibit child labour or forced labour. In order to prevent hiring child labour or forced labour, the Human Resource Department conducts a background check of all job applicants under the Background Check Policy to verify their identities and age during the recruitment process. We strictly comply with relevant labour laws and regulations in places of operations. In case of any instance of child employment, we would immediately terminate the contract.

During the reporting period, the Group was not aware of any non-compliance with relevant laws and regulations 3 that have a significant impact on the Group relating to preventing child and forced labour. There were no reported cases of child or forced labour during the reporting period.

The Group acknowledges the importance of empowering employees with professional knowledge and skills to help them reach their full potential. It not only helps employees to stay competitive in the fast-growing industry, but also meets the Group's development goals. To this end, we invest solid resources in employee training and development.

A Group Training and Development Policy is in place and the responsibility for its implementation has been assigned to relevant personnel and departments who oversee the development of training strategy and to make training an integral part of our operations. Department heads, department managers and station managers are assigned to arrange appropriate internal training for employees in their respective departments. The Human Resources Manager is responsible to keep a training record and to review training and development recommendations from various departments and employees regularly, so as to better assist employees in achieving their professional development goals. We provide various in-house training programmes as follows:

Mandatory Training | A New Employee Orientation programme is provided to all newly hired regular full time staff to get an overall view on the Company and the job position. The contents include the history of the Group, the structure of the local station and own department, introduction to all departments and the employee's job responsibility.
On-the-job Training | Offered by related department and led by department heads. The learning status, such as quality and quantity of work, familiarity with in-house systems is supervised by senior staff.
Training on In-house Systems | The IT Department and the Accounts Department provide training classes for employees regarding various in-house IT systems whenever appropriate.
Others | Including but not limited to ESG reporting and carbon disclosure training.

To inspire employees to acquire new knowledge and keep abreast of the latest trends in the logistics industry, we encourage employees to participate in external training programmes based on their job needs and promote a comprehensive learning environment in the workplace. The Performance Appraisal System helps department managers to identify and confirm employees who need training. We select suitable staff to participate in job-related external courses, seminars and workshops, according to their positions and needs. During the year, we arranged both internal and external training sessions for our employees with various themes including dangerous goods, cargo operation, warehouse in/out procedures and regulated agent regime.

A Staff Training Scheme is established for employees to apply for training subsidies and reimbursement for external courses and programmes that are related to their job positions or future work assignments. We also conduct evaluations after both internal and external training upon completion, so as to ensure their relevance and effectiveness.
During the reporting period, the Group had a total of 305 training hours and 168 employees were trained, accounting for 62% of the total workforce.
We organise Dangerous Goods Regulations training by external parties to for our airfreight operation staff, ensuring they are qualified for handling dangerous goods shipments. The training includes:
■ Reference IATA Dangerous Goods Regulations manual
■ Choose the appropriate container for air transportation
■ Pack dangerous goods correctly
■ Prepare documentation and labelling

In order to create a safe and healthy working environment and reduce the occupational safety risk to the lowest level, we have aligned health and safety policies and the ESG and ISO management system, as to ensure all business operations align with occupational health and safety standards. Fire facilities and condition of emergency exit inspection are carried out regularly every half year. The Group did not record any case regarding work-related fatalities or work injuries. To protect employees from occupational injuries, we have appropriate equipment in place. The fire drill is conducted annually for all the frontlines employees.

We value both the physical and mental health of our employees, launching different activities to promote our employees' well-being as well as workplace safety. To reinforce employees' safety awareness and to equip them with necessary safety knowledge, we have formulated a set of occupational health and safety guidelines for frontline staff in warehouse operations and conduct safety training sessions regularly. During the year, 51% of the total workforce participated in safety training, accounting for a total of 333 safety training hours and 140 person-times.

We strictly comply with relevant laws and regulations. During the reporting period, the Group was not aware of any non-compliance with relevant laws and regulations 4 that have a significant impact on the Group relating to the provision of a safe working environment and protection of employees from occupational hazards. There were no work-related fatalities occurred in each of the past three years including the reporting year.

An effective supply chain management is critical for our business. Air freight as well as ocean freight services involve various vendors including airline companies, shipping line companies, carriers, co-loaders, transportation companies and related business agents. The Group values its relationships with suppliers and puts in efforts to maintain long-term and stable business relations. A Vendor Committee is formed by the top management team, corporate function heads, stations management heads and departmental management heads, to oversee and ensure smooth vendor selection and appointment. Our Vendor Management Policy offers guidelines on procurement of services and products from third parties.

We are aware of the importance of managing environmental and social risks of our supply chain. To this end, we improve ESG performance along the value chain and encourage suppliers and contractors to embed ESG standards and align with our Environmental and Social Responsibility Policy and Code of Conduct.

In order to reduce the ESG risks in the supply chain, we carry out due diligence in the supplier selection process. During procurement, we invite more than one quotation and conduct detailed background checks. We take social and environmental performance in aspects such as environmental protection, occupational health and safety and quality assurance etc., into consideration in the process of supplier selection. We also assign department managers to monitor vendors' performance regularly. An annual assessment review is conducted to ensure services or product quality of existing suppliers are in line with the Group's standards and expectations.
During the reporting period, the Group had 685 suppliers in total, of which approximately 87% were located in Asia.

Striving to provide safe and on-time delivery of goods to customers, we are certified for the ISO9001:2015 Quality Management Systems standard. The Operation Workflow Manual is in place and updated regularly, laying out managing work procedures on air freight and ocean freight to improve our quality performance.

Safety and security are viewed as the top priority. We inspect parcels carefully to avoid any hidden dangerous cargoes and make sure we comply with the strict limitations and controls on dangerous goods, so as to avoid any harm to public safety. A series of procedures are defined to facilitate special cargo handling including dangerous cargoes, commodities including batteries, temperature sensitive cargoes and wooden packing materials.
■ At least two persons with licenses handle DG cargoes
■ Only licensed holders are allowed to handle the documentation and cargoes
■ Labelling, packing instructions and markings on the cargoes should strictly follow the specific requirements
■ Check battery nature and the corresponding safety information before handling
■ Pass to DG Regulations certified persons to handle it as DG cargoes
■ Ensure all documentation, handling procedures and ability of the carrier meet our DG handling requirements
■ Check carefully the type of cargoes and the temperature required
■ Arrange refrigerated container when needed, ensure a good and precise control on the temperature for the entire voyage
■ Appoint certified fumigation vendors to conduct fumigation
■ Obtain fumigation certificate from vendor before delivering the cargo to sea freight warehouse

We use proper labelling on incoming cargoes for easy identification. There are various types of labels to indicate information about the goods such as quantity, origin and destination. We ensure these labels are visible and must not cover customers' labels or marking.

Understanding and appreciating customers' needs and enhancing customer satisfaction are important issues. We collect customer feedback and opinions in terms of service quality, on time delivery, time management and employees' performance regularly via different communication channels including customer site visits.

During the reporting period, the Group was not aware of any non-compliance with relevant laws and regulations 5 that have a significant impact on the Group relating to health and safety, advertising, labelling and privacy matters relating to products and services provided and methods of redress.

The Group protects intellectual property rights of both itself and third parties. The Corporate Human Resources Department is responsible for providing guidelines on protecting intellectual property rights, and managing related assets such as logos, patents, trademarks and service marks, domain names, copyrights for both hardware and software etc. The use of all copyrighted materials of the Group should be authorised by the Corporate HR Department. As stated in the Code of Conduct, all employees who have the right to access or control proprietary information are required to prevent abuse or misuse by applying adequate protection measures.

We strictly comply with relevant laws and regulations in Hong Kong and Mainland China. To protect the security and data privacy of our customers, all collected information concerning customers and other companies is kept confidential and hard copies are required to be shredded before disposal. During the reporting period, the Group was not involved in any litigation relating to infringement of any intellectual rights.

The Group is committed to upholding high moral and ethical principles and conducting business with due regard to integrity, impartiality and honesty. We have zero tolerance for illegal acts and any forms of corruption including bribery, extortion, fraud and money laundering. We have formulated a series of anti-corruption policies listed below to regulate employees' actions and strengthen their awareness with regard to anti-corruption.
Please refer to the section headed 'Applicable Laws and Regulations' for Product Responsibility-related laws and regulations.
■ Provide instructions regarding legal compliance, soliciting, accepting and offering advantages

■ The acts of soliciting or accepting any advantages from clients, suppliers, agents, co-loaders or any persons in connection with the business of the Group are prohibited, unless permission has been obtained from the Group

■ Under no circumstance may bribes or similar considerations be offered to any person or company for the purpose of influencing these parties for obtaining or retaining business or directing business to the Group

■ Care must be taken to avoid any possible conflict of interest in the provision or acceptance of entertainment or gifts, to prevent the situation from being perceived or construed as providing or receiving an incentive for any commercial transaction
■ Encourage employees to report any suspicious concerns regarding misconduct or malpractices within the Group through the whistleblowing mechanism
■ The identity of the whistle-blower is kept confidential in the whole reporting and investigation process
■ All cases are reviewed under fair and independent investigation followed by appropriate follow-up actions

The Group strictly complies with anti-corruption-related laws and regulations. During the reporting period, the Group was not aware of any non-compliance with relevant laws and regulations 6 that have a significant impact on the Group relating to bribery, extortion, fraud and money laundering. The Group was not involved in any corruption cases in the reporting year.

We are dedicated to supporting the communities where we operate by means of investing in community affairs and functions, to fulfill the Group's corporate social responsibility. During the year, we put in efforts on long-term community investment strategy, aiming to make use of our expertise and network to support sustainable development in the communities as well as serving the needs of the underprivileged.

In order to promote a caring culture within the Group, we encourage employees to participate in a wide range of volunteering activities, seeking opportunities to collaborate with non-governmental organisations to further engage in community services. In 2021, We partnered with the Hong Kong Young Women's Christian Association to distribute health kits to 200 underprivileged families to practice and promote the concept of 'Creating Shared Value'.
